account:
BenevolentAI researchers reported in February 2020 that their knowledge graph had helped them identify baricitinib, an arthritis drug, as a possible treatment for COVID-19. They proposed clinical testing after reviewing its effects on inflammation and proteins involved in viral entry.

In ACTT-2, 1,033 hospitalized adults received remdesivir with either baricitinib or a placebo. Median recovery took 7 days with baricitinib and 8 days with the placebo. In November 2020, reviewers at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) concluded that it was reasonable to believe that the benefits of baricitinib with remdesivir outweighed its risks, although the ACTT-2 mortality result was not statistically significant. The FDA authorized the combination for emergency use on 19 November 2020.

COV-BARRIER enrolled 1,525 adults. By day 28, 8% of patients receiving baricitinib had died, compared with 13% receiving a placebo. Both groups received standard care. Mortality was a secondary outcome. The trial did not meet its primary outcome of reduced disease progression, so its mortality result was not conclusive under the planned procedure for multiple comparisons. The results were published on 1 September 2021.

On 14 January 2022 the World Health Organization strongly recommended baricitinib for patients with severe or critical COVID-19. The FDA approved the COVID-19 indication on 10 May 2022. The subsequent RECOVERY trial enrolled 8,156 patients, and its results were published on 28 July 2022. Mortality, its primary outcome, was 12% with baricitinib and 14% with usual care alone. In Europe, Eli Lilly and Company withdrew its application on 7 December 2022 after the European Medicines Agency reached the provisional opinion that three trials did not conclusively show meaningful benefit.

fields.account:
BenevolentAI researchers reported in February 2020 that their knowledge graph had helped them identify baricitinib, an arthritis drug, as a possible treatment for COVID-19. They proposed clinical testing after reviewing its effects on inflammation and proteins involved in viral entry.

In ACTT-2, 1,033 hospitalized adults received remdesivir with either baricitinib or a placebo. Median recovery took 7 days with baricitinib and 8 days with the placebo. In November 2020, reviewers at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) concluded that it was reasonable to believe that the benefits of baricitinib with remdesivir outweighed its risks, although the ACTT-2 mortality result was not statistically significant. The FDA authorized the combination for emergency use on 19 November 2020.

COV-BARRIER enrolled 1,525 adults. By day 28, 8% of patients receiving baricitinib had died, compared with 13% receiving a placebo. Both groups received standard care. Mortality was a secondary outcome. The trial did not meet its primary outcome of reduced disease progression, so its mortality result was not conclusive under the planned procedure for multiple comparisons. The results were published on 1 September 2021.

On 14 January 2022 the World Health Organization strongly recommended baricitinib for patients with severe or critical COVID-19. The FDA approved the COVID-19 indication on 10 May 2022. The subsequent RECOVERY trial enrolled 8,156 patients, and its results were published on 28 July 2022. Mortality, its primary outcome, was 12% with baricitinib and 14% with usual care alone. In Europe, Eli Lilly and Company withdrew its application on 7 December 2022 after the European Medicines Agency reached the provisional opinion that three trials did not conclusively show meaningful benefit.
fields.summary: BenevolentAI researchers used the Benevolent Platform's knowledge graph to identify baricitinib for COVID-19, and in the RECOVERY trial mortality was 12% with the drug and 14% with usual care alone.

segment: Hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring supplemental oxygen or ventilatory support
summary: BenevolentAI researchers used the Benevolent Platform's knowledge graph to identify baricitinib for COVID-19, and in the RECOVERY trial mortality was 12% with the drug and 14% with usual care alone.
taxonomy_note: The clinical benefit is reduced mortality and faster recovery. AI assisted the researchers who proposed the drug for testing.
title: Baricitinib, identified with BenevolentAI's knowledge graph, lowered COVID-19 deaths in the RECOVERY trial
